_review_checklist: Compare every line against the photograph, not against the app.
Chord rows are monospaced: a chord's character column IS its position, so keep the alignment when you edit a lyric.
Write chords exactly as the page prints them - em, H7, -7, fiszm. Storage spelling is the app's job, not this file's.
warnings holds slugs, not prose: low-resolution, show-through-removed, two-songs, no-chords, german-chords, nothing-legible.
Put your name in reviewed_by when the text matches the page.
_notes: Chord columns are measured per character, not snapped to the start of a word. An earlier version of this file did snap them, which put the first C of verse 1 at column 9 (`szívedbe`'s first letter) when the page prints it at column 13, over the `e`. Robert caught it.
Floor, not round, when converting a pixel x to a column: a glyph starting at x sits inside the character whose cell contains x. Rounding moved that same C to column 14.
Eight chords were never recognised and were measured off the image against a pixel ruler: the C on every `Mi az…` and `Nézi…` line, plus verse 4's leading G.
The chords float at fixed horizontal positions and do not track the words. Verse 1's D sits over `lát!`; verse 2's over `szemedbe`. That is what the page does.
Verse 1 alone wraps its last chord in brackets: `G - C - D - ( C )`. Verses 2-4 print `G - C - D - C`.
No book number anywhere on the page. The title appears only in the phone's app bar, which is chrome rather than song content.

Both warnings are deliberately unticked: this is a born-digital screenshot, perfectly legible, with no reverse page to show through. Both currently fire, which is the point of recording them as unexpected.
